## Excursions from Puerto Río Tranquilo: Marble Caves or San Rafael?

[Puerto Río Tranquilo](/chile/place/puerto-rio-tranquilo/) is a small settlement beside [General Carrera Lake](/chile/place/general-carrera-lake/) on Chile's Carretera Austral. From here you can plan two different nature excursions: a trip to the nearby marble arches on the lake, or a much longer journey towards Patagonia's glaciers.

Our two routes differ in more than duration. They use different types of water transport, visit different areas, have distinct purposes and face different weather restrictions. Decide first whether you want to see light playing through marble vaults or the icy front of San Rafael, and only then plan your overnight stays.

## A private boat to the Marble Caves

The [Marble Caves by Private Boat excursion](/chile/marble-caves/marble-caves-private-boat-two-half-hours/) starts with a morning departure at approximately 07:00. It lasts 2.5 hours. The boat travels among natural stone arches and cavities formed by water acting on marble over many years.

The [Marble Caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/), also known as Capillas de Mármol, are on General Carrera Lake. The colour of the water and reflections changes with light, waves and season. The excursion provides a **private boat**, but that does not justify promising calm winds, entry beneath every arch or operation in all weather.

For this outing, bring protection from wind and spray, keep your camera in a protective case and consider boarding conditions. The boat trip's short duration does not mean another excursion can be scheduled without allowing for the approach, waiting time and possible weather delays.

## San Rafael Glacier via Exploradores Valley

The [San Rafael Glacier excursion](/chile/puerto-rio-tranquilo/san-rafael-exploradores-boat-full-day/) takes a full day, approximately from 08:00 to 18:00. Travellers first drive through [Exploradores Valley](/chile/place/exploradores-valley/) to a bay, then board a boat and continue towards San Rafael Lagoon.

The destination is [San Rafael Glacier](/chile/place/san-rafael-glacier/) and a boat journey among floating ice. This is a different part of [Laguna San Rafael National Park](/chile/place/laguna-san-rafael-national-park/) with considerably more extensive travel logistics. According to the itinerary, you return to Puerto Río Tranquilo later that day.

Glacier visibility and navigational possibilities vary with the weather. Do not promise a particular distance to the ice wall, a fixed number of icebergs or an unconfirmed close approach.

| Feature | Marble Caves | San Rafael |
|---|---|---|
| Duration | 2.5 hours | Full day |
| Main attraction | Marble arches | Glacier |
| Format | Private boat | Boat excursion |
| Logistics | Lake | Valley and lagoon |

## How many days should you spend in the village?

If you only want to visit the Marble Caves, the excursion takes a relatively small part of a day, but strong winds on the exposed lake can change plans. San Rafael needs a separate full day. To visit both, it is better to schedule them on different days so their order can be adjusted if conditions change.

Chile's tourism portal separately describes the Marble Caves as an excursion from Puerto Río Tranquilo and confirms access to San Rafael Lagoon through this area. Our excursions, however, follow their individual programme conditions: **prices, tickets, meals and exact services cannot be inferred from a general tourism guide**.

On an extended Patagonia itinerary, allowing enough time for Carretera Austral and overnight stays between remote places is more important than trying to see every attraction in one day. For other nature destinations, browse our [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and [nature journeys in Chile](/interests/wildlife/tours/chile/).

## Frequently asked questions about excursions from Puerto Río Tranquilo

### Can you see the Marble Caves by private boat?

Yes. This format and a duration of 2.5 hours are explicitly stated in the [current excursion programme](/chile/marble-caves/marble-caves-private-boat-two-half-hours/).

### Is San Rafael Glacier on the same short boat route?

No. The [San Rafael excursion](/chile/puerto-rio-tranquilo/san-rafael-exploradores-boat-full-day/) includes an overland transfer through Exploradores and a separate boat journey to the lagoon, occupying almost the entire day.

### Can both excursions be completed in a single day?

Together, the two programmes take substantially longer than an ordinary sightseeing day. For a reliable itinerary, schedule them on separate dates and allow for weather restrictions.

### Why might the timing of a boat excursion change?

Wind, waves and navigational safety affect sailings both on the lake and near glaciers. The actual departure is confirmed for the specific date.

## San Rafael Glacier: travelling through Exploradores Valley and by boat

[San Rafael Glacier](/chile/place/san-rafael-glacier/) is in Chilean Patagonia. Its ice front reaches a lagoon where icebergs and smaller broken blocks can float. The journey brings together two natural landscapes: green valleys with riverbeds and mountain slopes, and cold water beside an enormous mass of ice.

The Ada Tours excursion takes **a full day, approximately 08:00–18:00**. It starts and ends in [Puerto Río Tranquilo](/chile/place/puerto-rio-tranquilo/). Travellers first drive through Exploradores Valley to the bay of the same name, then board a boat for the crossing to San Rafael Lagoon.

## Exploradores Valley: the overland portion

On the way to the bay, you see mountain slopes and a valley shaped by glacial processes. This is a particularly clear example of how water, ice and mountains affect the surrounding landforms.

The drive **is not a separate hike on Exploradores Glacier**. Our route includes an overland transfer through the valley and a boat excursion to San Rafael. It does not include icefield trekking, crampon rental or any other mountaineering equipment.

Current restrictions also matter: Chile's conservation agency CONAF has announced **a closure of access to the front of Exploradores Glacier** for safety reasons. That applies to a different land-based area. Boat visits to San Rafael Lagoon follow their own access rules and weather conditions.

## Boat excursion to the glacier and icebergs

From Exploradores Bay, the boat heads towards the lagoon. As it approaches, the appearance of the water and shores changes and floating blocks of ice may appear. At the glacier, the contrast between bluish cracks in the ice, grey rocks and dark water is particularly striking.

The size and number of icebergs vary: the glacier is constantly moving, while water and wind affect where detached blocks float. **Approaching the ice front is subject to safety requirements**, so a specific distance from the glacier cannot be promised in advance. Keep a safe distance from large icebergs and follow crew instructions.

This is a journey through a natural glacial landscape, not a guarantee of witnessing an ice-calving event. Large blocks can detach without warning and pose a risk to vessels nearby.

## Weather and preparing for the trip

Patagonian wind, rain and temperatures can significantly affect the excursion. On the boat, the cold feels more intense than in the sheltered valley. Bring a waterproof hooded jacket, warm clothing, gloves, non-slip shoes and protection for your camera against spray.

Whether the boat can depart and reach the lagoon depends on current route conditions. In bad weather, the organiser may change or cancel the waterborne section for safety reasons. Leave some flexibility in the following day's schedule.

The separate price, guide language and meal arrangements need to be confirmed when planning. They should not be assumed to be included merely because the excursion lasts a whole day.

## San Rafael on a Chilean Patagonia itinerary

Unlike road-based sightseeing days in [Torres del Paine](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/torres-del-paine-standard-milodon-full-day/), this experience centres on **the boat trip through glacial waters**. Both are in Patagonia, but in different areas, and travel between them must be planned separately.

Compare other [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) if you would like to combine glaciers with lakes, national parks and mountain routes.

## Frequently asked questions about the San Rafael boat excursion

### Where does the excursion start?

In **Puerto Río Tranquilo**. Travellers first drive through Exploradores Valley, then board the boat at the bay.

### How long does the route take?

The published programme gives an approximate time of **08:00–18:00**.

### Does the boat go right up to the ice wall?

The crew, weather and safety requirements determine the distance. A close approach to the ice front is not guaranteed.

### Is a walk on Exploradores Glacier included?

No. The itinerary includes a drive through the valley and **a boat trip to San Rafael**, without hiking on Exploradores Glacier.

## Tours featuring the boat excursion to San Rafael Glacier

The [San Rafael Glacier boat excursion through Exploradores Valley](/chile/puerto-rio-tranquilo/san-rafael-exploradores-boat-full-day/) is included in a [3-day journey through Aysén](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/), a [9-day Chile tour](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) and a [16-day Bolivia and Chile itinerary](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/). These journeys share a day in nature, but their geography before and after it differs.

The excursion's defining feature is the combination of an overland transfer, a boat trip and natural restrictions. This is not a short stroll between city sights: visiting San Rafael Lagoon requires an entire day and allowance for possible weather changes.

## How the day through Exploradores works

The route starts in [Puerto Río Tranquilo](/chile/place/puerto-rio-tranquilo/), continues through [Exploradores Valley](/chile/place/exploradores-valley/) and reaches [Exploradores Bay](/chile/place/exploradores-bay/). Travellers board a boat and head towards the lagoon, where [San Rafael Glacier](/chile/place/san-rafael-glacier/) and drifting icebergs come into view. The standalone excursion takes approximately **08:00–18:00**.

[Laguna San Rafael National Park](/chile/place/laguna-san-rafael-national-park/) is connected to the Northern Patagonian Ice Field. Its sectors have different means of access. This itinerary includes **a boat excursion to the lagoon**, not an overland hike on Exploradores Glacier.

CONAF has reported closure of access to the front of Exploradores Glacier because of ice instability. This restriction applies to a different activity and does not automatically cancel all boat navigation to San Rafael. Actual permission for the boat to depart, weather conditions and route accessibility must nevertheless be confirmed before travelling.

## Which tour should you choose?

| Duration | What else is included |
|---|---|
| [3 days](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/) | Marble Caves, Aysén |
| [9 days](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) | Atacama, Torres del Paine |
| [16 days](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) | Bolivia, Uyuni, Chile |

**Three days in Patagonia.** The [short programme](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/) begins at Balmaceda Airport. Day 1 involves driving along the [Carretera Austral](/chile/place/carretera-austral/) to [General Carrera Lake](/chile/place/general-carrera-lake/) and Puerto Río Tranquilo. Day 2 is the San Rafael boat trip, and day 3 covers the [Marble Caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/) and the return drive towards the airport. Two nights are spent in Puerto Río Tranquilo. This is a compact Aysén-focused itinerary.

**Nine days in Chile.** On [this itinerary](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/), San Rafael is visited on day 6. Travellers first explore northern Atacama and then move on to Aysén. The boat day is followed by the Marble Caves and a separate [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) excursion. This programme involves substantially more transfers between regions.

**Sixteen days in Bolivia and Chile.** The [longer route](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) adds high-altitude Bolivia, the Uyuni Salt Flat, Atacama, Santiago and southern Patagonia. Day 11 is dedicated to San Rafael. It suits those who want to combine several natural regions and are comfortable with a longer trip.

A shared excursion name does not make the three journeys identical products. Duration, hotels, transport between regions, included meals and guiding arrangements are specified by each individual tour.

## Weather, clothing and allowing spare time

At the glacier lagoon, wind, rain and cold conditions are possible even when northern Chile is warm. Waterproof clothing, a warm layer, non-slip shoes and protection for belongings against water are useful. Discuss any personal mobility restrictions in advance for boarding the vessel.

**Boat departures depend on the weather.** This is explicitly stated in the 16-day programme. Every day of the 3-day tour is allocated to travel or an excursion, so it does not automatically include a spare day. If the glacier is the main reason for your trip, discuss possible extra time before buying flights; rescheduling options and related costs must be agreed separately.

For other nature itineraries, explore [all Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and the [nature travel collection for Chile](/interests/wildlife/tours/chile/). Check that the actual programme includes San Rafael: visiting another Patagonian glacier is not equivalent.

## Frequently asked questions about tours to San Rafael

### Is this a boat excursion or a glacier hike?

The route features a boat trip to San Rafael Lagoon via Exploradores. Hiking on Exploradores Glacier is not included.

### Can you combine San Rafael and the Marble Caves in 3 days?

Yes. The [3-day programme](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/) visits these attractions on separate days, with road and boat sections between them.

### Which tours include both San Rafael and Torres del Paine?

Both regions feature in the [9-day Chile itinerary](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) and the [16-day Bolivia–Chile journey](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/).

### Is a boat departure guaranteed in all weather?

No. Navigation depends on water conditions, weather and current restrictions. Discuss how possible changes to the programme will be managed before travelling.

### How long is the standalone excursion?

It takes a full day, approximately 08:00–18:00, including the road transfer and boat section.

## Petrohué and Osorno: a private day trip from Puerto Varas

[Puerto Varas](/chile/place/puerto-varas/) is a convenient base for two recognisable natural attractions in Chile's Lake District: [Petrohué Falls](/chile/place/petrohue-waterfalls/) and [Osorno Volcano](/chile/place/osorno-volcano/). Both lie in the area of [Vicente Pérez Rosales National Park](/chile/place/vicente-perez-rosales-national-park/), but the experiences are different. At Petrohué, rushing water crosses volcanic rock; at Osorno, a snow-capped volcanic cone rises above lakes and forests.

Ada Tours offers **a private excursion after breakfast, returning to Puerto Varas in the evening**. The itinerary centres on park landscapes, a walk on designated trails in the Petrohué area and a continuation towards Osorno. It is a day in nature, without a stated technical ascent of the volcano.

## Petrohué: why the water and rocks look unusual

The [Petrohué River](/chile/place/petrohue-river/) flows through landscapes shaped by volcanic activity. At the falls, currents cross dark rock ledges, with pale or turquoise water standing out against stone and greenery. The route includes a walk along the river and views of the forest.

The exact visit depends on whether the sector is open and the state of the paths. **Information about access to Saltos del Petrohué as of 18 October 2026 was conflicting:** the CONAF page retained a notice of closure since 30 September for infrastructure maintenance, while a Puerto Varas municipal update dated 9 October said the falls were open. Obtain current confirmation from the park administration before departing. A viewpoint or entry into a closed sector cannot be promised in advance.

If access to the falls is restricted, nearby nature views are not automatically an equivalent replacement: changes to the programme must be agreed.

## Osorno: a volcano without a compulsory climb

[Osorno](/chile/place/osorno-volcano/) is a major landmark of southern Chile. In clear weather, its snowy summit rises above lakeshores; clouds may hide it completely. This excursion continues towards the volcano and explores the surrounding landscapes.

**An ascent to the crater, skiing activities and the cable car are not specified as part of this excursion.** This is significant when choosing: a trip to the foothills or viewpoints and a mountaineering ascent have entirely different requirements.

CONAF issues separate safety warnings for the volcano. Ordinary precautions are appropriate for open viewpoints; higher mountain trails, if planned at all, need separate organisation, access permission and equipment.

## How to arrange the day in the Lake District

Puerto Varas lies on Llanquihue Lake and makes a good base for the excursion. The drive towards the national park, stops along the river and onward journey to Osorno all take time. Treat this as **a full day in nature**, rather than automatically adding another distant excursion afterwards.

On our [33-day South American Grand Tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/), the Petrohué and Osorno day follows arrival in Puerto Varas. This gives southern Chile's volcanoes their own stage of the journey rather than viewing them in passing between flights.

This route differs from trips centred on Todos los Santos Lake and Peulla. Its core is **the national park, river, waterfalls and Osorno Volcano**; neither a lake crossing nor a continuation across the border is stated.

## When to go and what to bring

Southern Chile is wet, and volcano visibility depends heavily on cloud cover. Bring several clothing layers, a rain jacket, non-slip shoes and protection for your camera. Heavy rain may change road conditions and access to park sectors.

The price and exact admission tickets are arranged separately. **The excursion is private, but transport details, guiding services and meals need confirmation** as part of the specific Ada Tours offer.

## Frequently asked questions about Petrohué and Osorno

### Is this one excursion or two different trips?

This product combines Petrohué and Osorno in one private day trip from Puerto Varas. The sequence can change depending on which sectors are accessible.

### Can you currently visit Petrohué Falls?

As of 18 October 2026, the official CONAF page and the municipal update presented contradictory information. Access needs separate confirmation before departure; visits to viewpoints cannot be guaranteed.

### Does the excursion include climbing Osorno?

No. The published programme describes travelling to the volcano and viewing it, without a mountaineering ascent.

### Where does the trip start and end?

It departs from and returns to Puerto Varas, with several natural stops during the day.

## Excursions to Puna Pau on Easter Island

[Puna Pau Quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/) lies in the central part of [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/). Red volcanic tuff was quarried here for *pukao*, cylindrical stone headdresses seen on some moai. The stop reveals another side of Rapa Nui technology and artistic tradition, beyond the island's famous coastal platforms.

Ada Tours excursions generally combine Puna Pau with [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) and [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/). It is therefore best to approach this selection as **a choice of short cultural routes through several monuments**, rather than a single ticket to the quarry alone.

## How the available excursions differ

[Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau](/chile/easter-island/ahu-akivi-puna-pau-tour/) is a compact excursion of approximately 4 hours. It visits the Ahu Akivi platform with its seven moai, then Puna Pau and a viewpoint towards Hanga Roa and the coast. Tahai is not listed in this version.

[Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-akivi-puna-pau-tahai/) is a private morning excursion to three archaeological areas. After the quarry, it continues to Tahai, including restored platforms and Ko Te Riku, with the moai's reconstructed eyes.

[Ahu Akivi, Hanga Pukure, Puna Pau and Tahai](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/) lasts 4 hours and is **a private excursion with an English-speaking guide**. In addition to Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai, it includes the unrestored Hanga Pukure platform. A Russian-speaking guide is listed as an optional service for an additional charge.

[Easter Island: Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-akivi-puna-pau-tahai-visit/) is another route variant that includes Hanga Pukure. The places are listed, but whether the excursion is private and the guide's language must be confirmed separately.

| Itinerary | Distinctive feature |
|---|---|
| Ahu Akivi – Puna Pau | Without Tahai |
| Ahu Akivi – Tahai | Three main sites |
| With Hanga Pukure | Four stops |
| 'Easter Island' variant | Puna Pau and Tahai |

Similar names do not mean identical services or stops. Consider the guide's language, whether it is a group or private excursion, the places actually visited and time available to explore.

## What to see at the quarry itself

Most moai were carved from a different volcanic material, while pukao were made from Puna Pau's red tuff. The quarry contains stone blanks and traces of the craftsmen's work. The colour contrast helps explain how separate statue elements were transported to ceremonial platforms.

Nearby monuments complete the story. [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) is known for a row of seven restored moai facing towards the ocean. [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/) has several platforms near the shore. A short route therefore connects the making of statue elements with their installation at ceremonial sites.

## Access rules and preparation

Under the official Rapa Nui National Park regulations, protected sites require **a ticket and a guide accredited by the Ma'u Henua community**. Before travelling, confirm exactly which places the ticket covers and what guiding is included in your chosen excursion. A park ticket should not be treated as prepaid unless the excursion's terms say it is included.

At archaeological sites, visitors must remain on designated routes, must not touch moai and may not remove stones. Comfortable footwear, wind and sun protection and water are helpful on exposed slopes. This is a cultural heritage excursion, not a technical climb of volcanoes.

If you plan a full day on Rapa Nui, Puna Pau combines naturally with nearby central monuments; leave [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) and [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) for a separate longer island excursion.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions to Puna Pau

### Is there a short excursion visiting only Ahu Akivi?

Yes. The [Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau route](/chile/easter-island/ahu-akivi-puna-pau-tour/) confirms these as its main places and gives an approximate duration of 4 hours.

### Which programme includes Hanga Pukure?

The [private four-hour excursion](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/) explicitly includes the unrestored Hanga Pukure platform alongside Puna Pau and Tahai. Another published variant also describes this stop.

### On which excursion is the guide language specified?

For the [private trip including Hanga Pukure](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/), English guiding is confirmed; a Russian-speaking guide is available at additional cost.

### Do you need a national park ticket?

Park attractions require a ticket and accredited guide. Whether these are included in the price depends on the specific programme.
